=={{header|Cxc}}==

Ticker, Grid, and View run as three decoupled atoms. Grid stores live cells in a sparse <code>Set of Cell</code>, not a dense grid, and broadcasts <code>frame_ready</code> after each generation, with View subscribing.

<syntaxhighlight lang="elixir">
# My take on conway's game of life with OOP done right:
# explicit, decoupled and functional.

# cells are sparsely stored on the grid (Set of Cell, no dense array)
def Cell:
    x: Int!
    y: Int!

# common patterns used in other entries
def Patterns:
    glider:      Set of Cell = [Cell(1, 0), Cell(2, 1), Cell(0, 2), Cell(1, 2), Cell(2, 2)]
    blinker:     Set of Cell = [Cell(0, 0), Cell(1, 0), Cell(2, 0)]
    r_pentomino: Set of Cell = [Cell(1, 0), Cell(2, 0), Cell(0, 1), Cell(1, 1), Cell(1, 2)]
    -> running

# the clock. OOP has no imperative loops, so
# we use message dispatch for iteration instead.
def Ticker(ticks: Int!):
    count: Int! = 0

    -> running

    running <: step:
        |:  self.count >= self.ticks -> end
            :> died
        |?: -> running
            count => self.count + 1
            :> tick(n: self.count + 1)

def Grid(width: Int!, height: Int!):
    alive_cells: Set of Cell = []

    offsets: List of Cell = [Cell(-1, -1), Cell(0, -1), Cell(1, -1),
                             Cell(-1,  0),              Cell(1,  0),
                             Cell(-1,  1), Cell(0,  1), Cell(1,  1)]

    # `:-` denotes pure lazy computation
    # `=>` indicates a change in state.
    alive(x: Int!, y: Int!) :- self.alive_cells.contains(Cell(x, y))

    neighbors(x: Int!, y: Int!) :-
        self.offsets.map(o => self.alive(x + o.x, y + o.y).to_int()).sum()

    next_cell(x: Int!, y: Int!) :-
        self.neighbors(x, y) == 3 or (self.alive(x, y) and self.neighbors(x, y) == 2)

    next_alive :-
        range(self.width).seq().fold(self.alive_cells.empty(), (sx, x) =>
            range(self.height).seq().fold(sx, (sy, y) =>
                ||: self.next_cell(x, y) : sy.insert(Cell(x, y)) |?: sy))

    -> running

    running <: stamp(cells: Set of Cell, at_x: Int!, at_y: Int!) -> running
        alive_cells => cells.seq().fold(self.alive_cells,
            (acc, c) => acc.insert(Cell(c.x + at_x, c.y + at_y)))

    running <: advance_generation -> running
        alive_cells => self.next_alive
        :> frame_ready(cells: self.alive_cells, w: self.width, h: self.height)

def View:
    # notice this means we can scope side effects to the object
    use console: Console

    row_at(cells: Set of Cell, w: Int!, y: Int!) :-
        range(w).map(x => ||: cells.contains(Cell(x, y)) : "#" |?: ".").join("")

    -> running

    running <: show_frame(cells: Set of Cell, w: Int!, h: Int!) -> running
        range(h).for_each(y => console.write(self.row_at(cells, w, y)))
        console.write("")

def main:
    ticker: Ticker   = Ticker(20)
    g:      Grid     = Grid(12, 12)
    v:      View     = View()
    pat:    Patterns = Patterns()

    # start with a glider
    -> running
        |> g.stamp(cells: pat.glider, at_x: 1, at_y: 1)
        |> ticker.step()

    running <: ticker.tick(n: Int!) -> running
        |> g.advance_generation()

    running <: g.frame_ready(cells: Set of Cell, w: Int!, h: Int!) -> running
        |> v.show_frame(cells: cells, w: w, h: h)
        |> ticker.step()

    running <: ticker.died -> end
</syntaxhighlight>
